rules.when: The captain or task text explicitly requests Grok, the Grok CLI, harness=grok, or wording like 'send this to grok' / 'run on grok' / 'grok subagent'.
rules.why: Prompt-specified Grok override. Requires the Grok Build CLI installed and authenticated. Model omitted so grok uses its account default.

rules.when: The captain or task text explicitly requests Codex, harness=codex, or wording like 'send this to codex' / 'run on codex'.
rules.why: Prompt-specified Codex override. Requires the Codex CLI installed and authenticated.

rules.when: The captain or task text explicitly requests Claude, Claude Code, harness=claude, or wording like 'send this to claude' / 'run on claude' (and does not name Fable/Haiku).
rules.why: Prompt-specified Claude override defaults to Fable.

rules.when: The captain or task text explicitly requests Pi, harness=pi, or wording like 'send this to pi' / 'run on pi'.
rules.why: Prompt-specified Pi override. Pi is wrapped to Grok on this machine (bin/pi-grok); verify the exact model id with `pi` then `/model` and adjust here if it differs.

rules.when: The task is high-complexity technical or product design: architecture decisions, gnarly debugging, or work where depth and creativity matter more than speed.
rules.why: Ration the Claude subscription for exactly the tasks nothing else does as well (Fable only for high-complexity design).

rules.when: The task is a trivial mechanical edit such as a rote rename, formatting sweep, targeted typo fix, or simple file gathering.
rules.why: Cheapest fast profile for narrow, low-ambiguity work.

rules.when: The task is a big or ambiguous multi-file feature, a risky refactor, or work that requires holding many moving parts in mind.
rules.why: Strong profile for big ambiguous work; the array lets quota-array-dispatch fall through by live quota headroom across Claude, Pi-on-Grok, and Codex.
